title: Amenophis
summary: Amenophis is named in Cory, Ancient Fragments (1876, ed. Hodges), with a reign length or synchronism. Display only.
description: Added from the Cory import. Display only. Cory gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not a BC year this record can sort on, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Cory is display-only and gives none).

standby.note: Standby placement only, placed with "The Exodus from Egypt and the Red Sea Crossing" (a linked event of this person's life). The year is that record's sort year, taken as-is. No reign length or age was added or subtracted. It is not a sort year.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 129; Manetho, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: Josephus's list, the Amenophis who succeeds Armesses. Not the other two Amenophis lengths in this extract.

reign.date: “hold it in possession for thirteen years”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 131; Manetho, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: A prophecy, in this extract, that certain people would subdue Egypt and hold it for thirteen years. Not the biblical sojourn. The editorial footnote on p. 132 which says Osarsiph means Moses was not used to attach anyone to Moses.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 134; Manetho, ap. Josephus, Against Apion, book 1
reign.note: The exile of Amenophis, 'to continue from its beginning during the predestined thirteen years'. The same thirteen years as the prophecy on p. 131, in a second sentence.
